title: Requested dictation route is overwritten after fallback
user_impact: Fallback telemetry can underreport the user-selected provider and make Moonshine or other provider failures harder to explain.
root_cause: The start path resolved requested and actual routes, then stored the actual route in fields named requested_provider and requested_model_id.
recommended_fix: Split requested and actual fields in DictationStartOptions and persisted history. Keep requestedSelection in requested fields, resolved selection in actual fields, and make stop/transcribe use actual fields explicitly.
regression_guard: Rust compile coverage plus follow-up scenario test for Moonshine selected, fallback enabled, MLX or Parakeet actual route, and history showing requested Moonshine plus actual fallback.

title: Renderer IPC command contract is duplicated and stringly typed
user_impact: Adding or removing commands can drift across Electron, renderer wrappers, and the Rust sidecar without compile-time coverage.
root_cause: The migration kept a broad allowlist, a generic invoke API, and a large Rust match table as separate sources of truth.
recommended_fix: Introduce a single command catalog with command name, params, result type, timeout class, and renderer exposure. Generate or validate the Electron allowlist and TypeScript client from that catalog.
regression_guard: gate:ipc-contract validates renderer allowlist against sidecar dispatch. Remaining catalog generation is tracked separately.

title: Rust sidecar lib.rs is carrying too many runtime domains
user_impact: Small dictation, meeting, license, or IPC changes have high regression risk because unrelated flows share one 17k-line module.
root_cause: Command routing, app state, dictation lifecycle, meeting processing, platform paste, settings normalization, and tests are concentrated in one file.
recommended_fix: Extract command modules by domain, move dictation and meeting lifecycle state machines behind narrow services, and keep lib.rs as app composition plus command dispatch only.
regression_guard: Module-boundary tests for command registration and existing Rust tests moved with behavior unchanged.

title: Settings shell no longer blocks on backup scan but still starts too much first-load work
user_impact: First Settings open can still feel slow or jittery because permission, license, keychain, backup, and diarization probes start around initial render.
root_cause: The view has lazy sections, but several secondary probes are still mounted globally and compete with the first useful paint.
recommended_fix: Move permission, license, keychain, and diarization probes behind section-level loaders with independent loading and error states. Keep only getSettings in the critical path.
regression_guard: Secondary Settings loaders now have section-level timeout guards. Still needs packaged cold Settings timing artifact.

title: Dictation and Meetings views are oversized state containers
user_impact: Profile, routing, meeting notes, chat, recall, exports, and transcript editing regressions are likely because local state and effects are tightly coupled.
root_cause: Large views own domain state, persistence, UI rendering, async request guards, and telemetry formatting in one component.
recommended_fix: Split each view into a domain hook, command handlers, and presentational sections. Preserve behavior while making profile CRUD, route selection, and meeting detail independently testable.
regression_guard: Focused component tests for each extracted section and unchanged full-view smoke tests.

title: Dictation launch app matrix remains 1 of 16 verified
user_impact: The app cannot honestly claim broad system-wide dictation parity until packaged insertion evidence exists for target apps.
root_cause: Product behavior may be implemented, but launch certification is incomplete for most frozen macOS and Windows app targets.
recommended_fix: Run packaged insertion capture per matrix row, record scratch target evidence, fix delivery route failures, and only then update statuses.
regression_guard: Gate app-matrix plus per-app artifact verifier in CI or release checklist.

title: Windows packaged QA is still entirely blocked
user_impact: Dual-platform GA remains blocked even if macOS feels good locally.
root_cause: Windows install, capture, meetings, retention, export, backup, license, and signing rows have no passing packaged evidence.
recommended_fix: Execute the Windows handoff on a Windows release host, copy back artifacts, and fix product failures before signing.
regression_guard: Windows packaged QA runner plus gate:windows-handoff:verify and gate:qa-matrix.

title: Overlay visibility still has multiple owners
user_impact: Popup close and app focus bugs can reappear because Rust state, Electron window commands, and React window.hide can all change visibility.
root_cause: The previous fix added dismissed state, but ownership is still split across backend lifecycle state, Electron windows, and popup code.
recommended_fix: Create an overlay controller contract where backend emits state only, Electron owns window visibility, and React requests state transitions without hiding itself directly.
regression_guard: React popup no longer hides or shows its own window. Remaining backend and Electron ownership contract needs coverage.

title: Meeting overlay hides as soon as background processing begins
user_impact: Users may miss processing, transcript-refresh, or error state after stopping a meeting, which weakens the Granola-style trust UX.
root_cause: The stop path switches to processing, hides the overlay, then continues transcription in a detached task.
recommended_fix: Keep a visible processing state in the main meeting surface and optionally keep a compact overlay until transcript-first-available or failure. Make background task status resumable after restart.
regression_guard: Packaged meeting processing UX scenario that verifies spinner, status, transcript refresh, export readiness, and error recovery.

title: Audio callback paths can panic on poisoned mutexes
user_impact: A lock poisoning event in the audio thread can take down dictation instead of surfacing a recoverable error.
root_cause: Audio callback closures used lock().unwrap() in production capture paths.
recommended_fix: Replace unwraps with poison-safe handling that logs once, stops capture cleanly, and emits a user-facing recovery event.
regression_guard: Rust compile coverage now covers poison-safe callback helper usage. Follow-up can add direct poisoned-lock unit coverage.

title: One fixed 60 second IPC timeout covers every sidecar command
user_impact: Long model downloads, backups, repair actions, and live ASR probes can time out through the renderer even when the backend is still working.
root_cause: The IPC bridge lacked command classes, progress-aware commands, cancellation, and per-command timeout policy.
recommended_fix: Add timeout classes to the command catalog, use short timeouts for UI reads, long or progress-bound flows for downloads and backups, and return cancellable operation IDs for long work.
regression_guard: Vitest covers short, default, long, and extended timeout policy. Cancellable operation IDs remain a future enhancement.

title: Sidecar receives the full Electron process environment
user_impact: Secrets loaded into the Electron process are inherited by the sidecar and any sidecar child process, increasing blast radius.
root_cause: The sidecar spawn used env: process.env wholesale.
recommended_fix: Spawn the sidecar with an explicit allowlist for required runtime variables and prefer keychain or provider secret storage for cloud keys.
regression_guard: Vitest covers allowed runtime/provider variables and excludes unrelated token-shaped values.

title: Verification scripts still generate or rewrite artifacts
user_impact: Running gates can dirty the worktree and make it hard to tell product fixes from regenerated evidence.
root_cause: Some verify scripts also write output artifacts, and gate scripts mix generate and verify responsibilities.
recommended_fix: Split generate and verify commands, make verify commands read-only by default, and reserve writes for explicit refresh commands.
regression_guard: Doc-command hygiene check plus a script test that verify mode leaves git status unchanged.

title: Linux release targets remain configured even though GA excludes Linux
user_impact: Accidental Linux artifacts could create unsupported release expectations and extra security or signing obligations.
root_cause: The packaging config contained Linux targets while release docs and plans treat macOS and Windows as GA blockers.
recommended_fix: Mark Linux experimental, remove it from default release scripts, or require an explicit linux build script with no launch claims.
regression_guard: Release config now omits Linux targets from GA config. Follow-up can add a config assertion.

title: DownloadManager default can panic during app setup
user_impact: A missing or unwritable data path can crash setup instead of producing a repairable startup error.
root_cause: Default called Self::new().expect instead of returning an error through app initialization.
recommended_fix: Remove Default for fallible construction or make AppState::new return a typed setup error that the Electron shell can show.
regression_guard: Default now falls back to a temp model directory instead of panicking. Typed startup setup errors remain future hardening.

title: Settings still relies on broad event any casts
user_impact: Form regressions can slip through because change events and value coercion are not consistently typed.
root_cause: Large hand-written settings form uses repeated inline handlers with any.
recommended_fix: Introduce small typed setting controls for text, number, switch, select, and textarea fields, then remove broad event casts.
regression_guard: Typecheck plus component tests for representative controls.

title: Backend facade is still the main source for domain modules
user_impact: Dead-code cleanup is passing, but the frontend still depends on a large compatibility facade that slows future IPC cleanup.
root_cause: Domain modules re-export from a legacy backend file instead of owning narrow generated clients.
recommended_fix: Move command wrappers into domain modules, keep a temporary compatibility barrel only where needed, then delete the facade once imports are migrated.
regression_guard: Knip gate plus import-boundary test preventing new imports from the facade.
